```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(reindeer)
corp <- demo_corpus()
```

## Praat TextGrid and ELAN

`read_annotations()` and `write_annotations()` choose the format from the file
extension (`.TextGrid`, `.eaf`) and use one schema: `level`, `labels`, `start`,
`end`, with times in milliseconds, exactly like a `segment_list`.

```{r write}
segs <- query(corp, "Phonetic == V") |> collect()
tg <- tempfile(fileext = ".TextGrid")
write_annotations(segs, tg)
ann <- read_annotations(tg)
ann
```

```{r eaf}
eaf <- tempfile(fileext = ".eaf")
write_annotations(segs, eaf)
nrow(read_annotations(eaf)) == nrow(segs)
```

## Coming from emuR

reindeer reads and writes the same on-disk database, so a corpus made with
emuR opens directly and keeps working in emuR.

| emuR | reindeer |
|------|----------|
| `load_emuDB(path)` | `corpus(path)` |
| `query(db, "Phonetic == t")` | `query(corp, "Phonetic == t")` |
| `requery_hier()` / `requery_seq()` | `descend_to()` / `ascend_to()` / `move_to()` |
| `get_trackdata(db, seglist, "fms")` | `quantify(segs, <dsp function>)` |
| `serve(db)` | `annotate(corp)` |
| `list_bundles()` / `list_sessions()` | `get_metadata(corp)` |

Queries give the same results as emuR on the 80 golden test queries; the
difference is speed (the cache is synced incrementally and queries run as
a single SQL statement) and that results are tibbles with provenance
(`vignette("querying")`).
